answer.answer: Audit-ready takeover completed. The existing canonical snapshot remains unchanged; checkpoint `checkpoint:24440d8f-eeb6-6262-b565-61ed56028ddd` records the verified import boundary, selective promotion, supersession rules, and unresolved live-save questions.

claims.value: `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` was preserved losslessly with its verified extracted tree under Git-ignored `raw/`. The ZIP is 21,674,717 bytes with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`; it has 123 entries including directories and 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`. `unzip -t` and every packaged SHA-256 passed. The legacy SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, core delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script remain preserved only under `raw/`; tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` provide the audit trail.

The archive’s repeated attribution of numeric data to build `23761620` is corrected to a two-axis boundary. The source/game-data claim is Update 1 internal version `35118973`, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441`; the canonical capture is SRDB `2.3.4`, snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, captured 2026-07-11. Separately, the latest public executable observed at capture was Update 1 Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`; that executable observation does not establish the provenance of every numeric value. Imported numeric reports remain legacy calculations until rerun against the canonical snapshot.

The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantically duplicated by the richer RuptureOps corpus and were not installed as a competing game-data snapshot. Selective promotions were limited to `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`; six Ore Excavator v2 recipe/producer associations in `sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json`; explicit consumable-effect assumptions in `sources/consumable-effects.json`; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected the overwritten building-shaped `airlock` detail and Training Corporation’s literal `$undefined` index. No second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family, including its buffer-minimization study, five-output-depot bank, and overbuilt three-Stabilizer/two-slow-press direction, is superseded audit history and must not become current guidance without new evidence. The July 11 progression note is active authority, but its Flowworks build is an adopted plan—not confirmed construction: start with one Stabilizer, one Impeller, and one Turbine; add one Nozzle and two Valves; add two Pumps for the Pressure Tank stage; add the second Stabilizer before Scanner/levels 11–12; reserve one HRS v2 pad and build it only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. Exact live Corporation state and whether Flowworks or Grand Basin construction began remain unresolved.

answer.answer: The three dumps are preserved as exact provenance, while durable facts are promoted only once. Dump 01 adds no conversation content; Dumps 02 and 03 contribute distinct scaling/product and exploration/combat spans. The canonical state keeps installed facts, history, recommendations, questions, and plans in separate authority classes.

claims.value: All three user-authored dumps supplied on 2026-07-11 are preserved byte-identically. prompt-dump-01 is a semantic subset/formatting variant: lines 1-226 reproduce the prior factory-planning export and add no unique conversation content. prompt-dump-02 overlaps through lines 1-96 and has the unique span 99-249, covering scaling preferences, the app origin, installed-state corrections, freight conventions, and Cargo Dispatcher ideas. prompt-dump-03 overlaps in lines 2-91, repeats the final export request at line 229, and has the unique span 95-225, covering exploration, the Copperfield death, food observations, low-twitch combat constraints, and unresolved weapon/Yellowstone questions. The files are respectively 16,533 bytes/225 POSIX lines/SHA-256 a6534f50df6a09c98d6e3465488b60a60e5452a47cc2f63251df049c1cdc4be1; 25,263 bytes/251 lines/SHA-256 adde9855a1c3e439a02b6ccb243779ab29ed6a40602d15316caa369e1d90ec6d; and 16,411 bytes/228 lines/SHA-256 dc259be82ef89c908785b59644fa1f27f2be914c43f95f4f35351f94e1803a40.

Only direct first-person reports may support player state, history, preferences, and observations. Questions establish goals or uncertainty, not the truth of their premises. Quoted assistant text remains a recommendation and is not promoted as an independent player observation. An accepted plan remains distinct from installed or completed save state. Thus proposed construction, assistant advice, and unanswered research questions cannot become player facts merely because they occur in the preserved history.

The dumps lack original timestamps and come from overlapping conversation branches, so chronology uses explicit narrative ordering rather than reconstructed dates. Historical checkpoints do not silently overwrite current unknowns or prove the save has not advanced. Repeated statements strengthen provenance but remain one canonical fact: raw sources stay intact, while direct player facts and preferences are promoted once. No competing game-data snapshot or three competing save versions are created.

The canonical promoted outputs are: models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json for the best current installed-state model; models/rourke-update1-play-history__20260711.json for historical checkpoints, incidents, and durable player preferences; Player save - play history.md for the canonical human-readable gameplay timeline; and Player-derived product requirements.md for converting real play evidence into iOS requirements without declaring every idea an MVP feature. The baseline has profile_id rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711, as_of 2026-07-11, and explicitly separates planned sites and machines from confirmed construction. The earlier ZIP import remains canonical for its screenshots, generated reports, and more complete first factory-planning transcript.

claims.value: Active sites and durable roles as of 2026-07-11: Landerworks (`LW`) is the legacy Rotor, Stator, and Applicator exporter beside the initial lander. Sunstone Station (`LW-SA`) is its active satellite, supplying raw Calcium Ore and substantial solar generation. Faraday Works (`FW`) is the active rebuilt two-Core Titanium/Wolfram/Helium electrochem Works. answer.answer: Field brief: Little Cloud is a modest fight; Starry Night is easier. If storage is reasonably close, bank excess ammunition and consumables before moving. Otherwise, keep a recovery reserve, clear Little Cloud methodically, then continue to Starry Night and open its final chest before looting debris. The tagged chamber improves the respawn location but does not protect carried weapons or supply replacement gear.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty. Within 250 units it has 13 persistent hostile spawn entries: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder, with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers indicate possible persistent population, not 13 simultaneous attackers; the player later completed it and reported it was “no big deal.”

Bank excess ammunition and consumables first if returning to storage is reasonably quick. Otherwise preserve a reserve and proceed methodically through Little Cloud, using the nearby respawn only as a fallback, then continue to the lower-threat Starry Night.

A claimed Regeneration Chamber can shorten the return after death, but it does not provide replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, or rebuilding materials; Update 1 makes all carried weapons losable on death, so keep replacement gear in a separate safe cache. Direct field evidence from one Geo Scanner encounter shows corruption disabling a contested base and its chamber, causing respawn at the starting launcher, but the exact corruption threshold and universal chamber-disable rules remain unverified.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty, with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, though roaming enemies can still wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains an Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module; clear wanderers and open that chest before looting debris.

decisions: Recommend banking excess supplies when storage is reasonably close; otherwise preserve a reserve and proceed methodically.
Treat spawn markers as possible persistent population, not simultaneous attackers.
Treat corruption-related chamber failure as one observed encounter rather than a universal rule.
next_actions: Bank excess supplies if practical, clear Little Cloud, then proceed to Starry Night and open its final chest first.

answer.answer: Durable guidance now records the two-stage recovery failure, the powered-fire-base success, the limits of what the encounter proves, and the unresolved loot wording. Checkpoint committed as checkpoint:66edbebd-7488-6b37-e7b1-2d7e9991c6b7.

claims.value: The first Geo Scanner defense took three attempts. After the first death, the player respawned at a nearby claimed base that had no replacement weapons or materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks. On the second attempt, the temporary scanner fire base’s installed turrets were not powered; the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber, and the next respawn occurred at the starting launcher. The third attempt succeeded with a fully built-out fire base and every turret powered.

The successful intervention was to fully build out the scanner fire base and power every turret before activation. The automated defense then held, and the player described the turrets “singing” against the enemy as a strongly positive payoff after the frustrating failures.

Direct observation establishes only this encounter’s sequence: unpowered turrets provided no defense, the player was overwhelmed, and corruption disabled this fire base and its Regeneration Chamber. It does not establish a universal corruption threshold or every condition under which Regeneration Chambers are disabled; any broader mechanic remains unverified.

Future Geo Scanner checklist: stock the remote recovery point with replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials; keep a safe cache outside the contested base’s corruption failure domain; power and function-check every turret before activation; and plan the worst-case respawn and return route. The completed site appeared to yield two unusually good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving a quantity of 20, but the exact item identities and counts remain unresolved and must not be presented as confirmed.

It lies in the active western/southwestern production corridor rather than at Grand Basin to the north. Flowworks is only a proposed footprint, not a placed Core; Faraday is immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn” and east/southeast of Flowworks.

answer.answer: The Watch Session remains a conservative, local-first native iPhone MVP: show the next meaningful event clearly, distinguish predicted cycle mechanics from separately evidenced opportunities, and never imply safety or exactness that has not been validated. The complete canonical design source covered all four requested facets; no pointer-only evidence leads were needed. Checkpoint persisted as `checkpoint:bc4c2997-eb31-41a8-601b-37dbed369b33`.

claims.value: Authority and version boundary: the canonical evidence is version 1 of the Watch Session design, created and updated 2026-07-11. It is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`, released 2026-06-17, with SRDB `2.3.4` captured 2026-07-11. The working cycle is 54 minutes from local fire-wave impact to the next impact. Because Creepy Jar has not published an official numerical phase formula, this must remain a versioned community/game-data model—not an eternal official invariant—even though `starrupture.tools` and an independent runtime-reading mod strongly corroborate it. Internal warning boundaries and opportunity timing still require live Hotfix 0.2.8 validation across solo, hosted co-op, and dedicated-server play. Use `predicted`, `expected`, `favorable`, and `lower threat`, never `exact`, `safe`, or `guaranteed`; do not invent numerical accuracy. Confidence states are `Unsynced`, `Manual sync - predicted`, `Confirmed at one later transition`, `Drift suspected`, and `Cycle data changed - re-sync required`. Downgrade confidence after a large correction, device-clock change, model-version change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Player-facing timeline: retain the 54-minute engine cycle but present five meaningful states—Fire wave `0:00-0:30` (0:30, remain sheltered), Cooling `0:30-1:30` (1:00, remain sheltered), Recovery / quiet window `1:30-11:30` (10:00, lower ambient threat), World active `11:30-51:30` (about 40:00, ordinary enemies and ecology active), and Ruptura warning `51:30-54:00` (about 2:30, return, bank loot, and shelter). Manual synchronization starts at `0:00` when the fire wall reaches the player. The portrait hierarchy, entirely visible without scrolling, is: capability/confidence line; semantic hero state and huge monospaced countdown; explicit countdown target; threat instruction and one action sentence; at most two prioritized opportunity cards; then exact-time next events and the always-visible `Mute one cycle` and `Re-sync` controls. During recovery, the hero target is when ordinary Vermin are expected to return; during active ecology it is the next Ruptura or warning-phase start. Retain a proportional whole-cycle rail for orientation, but add minimum/equal-width labeled steps or a next-event list so short Fire wave and Cooling states never disappear. Color is atmospheric support only: text, symbols, borders, and instructions must carry meaning independently.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Opportunities are evidence-bearing, separately versioned facts—not automatic consequences of phase mechanics. Each `OpportunityWindow` stores an ID, start event or offset, end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. Initial candidates are: reduced ordinary POI population during Recovery (`Lower ambient threat - triggered encounters may persist`); Oxallop in early recovery while lakebeds are dry; Cave access, Quartz, and Glowcaps during Recovery without guaranteed respawn; Ignitium immediately after Cooling through Recovery with variable spawn rate; experimental Star Tears timing in late Recovery, including the choice to leave cooled Ignitium unharvested; variable Coralion/Vulpir egg opportunity after the wave; surface foliage and water described only as `Regrowth underway`; and Sulheart hidden until exact current timing is validated. Cards must state provenance such as confirmed, community-derived, player-observed, or experimental. The post-wave window is never guaranteed safety because Geo Scanner, monolith, infection, Base Core, scripted POI, and other triggered encounters can ignore the environmental cycle.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Alerts and native safety: enemy return and Ruptura require distinct sounds and haptics, while no alert may rely on color or audio alone. The default enemy-return ladder is 5 minutes (amber edge, `Finish or leave hard POIs`, short double haptic, optional tone, normal notification), 2 minutes (persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, optional notification), 1 minute (red instruction, emphasized seconds, stronger distinct cue, background notification off by default), 15 seconds (static danger border, large seconds, one final cue, no ticking), and the event (`ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING`, urgent triple cue, notification or explicitly armed alarm). Pre-Ruptura cues are optional 10 minutes, then 5 minutes, 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact; a player-selected exit buffer can instead produce `TURN BACK NOW`. Offer `Full`, `Haptic only`, and `Visual only`, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, preview, `Mute one cycle`, and never replay missed-cue backlogs after resume—collapse to the strongest current state. Store absolute timestamps, recompute `(now - anchor) modulo cycle duration` on resume, reschedule notifications after anchor/model/policy changes, and deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and restore it afterward; do not use background audio as keep-alive. A Live Activity represents only the currently armed event. AlarmKit on iOS 26 may break through Silent mode and Focus, but requires authorization and a clear usage description and must be created only after an explicit `Arm loud enemy-return alarm` or Watch Session action—never as an endless 54-minute alarm. Earlier systems use normal local notifications; Time Sensitive is separately opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Keep capability status, `Next alert at …`, `Re-sync`, and `Mute one cycle` visible. Support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Reduce Motion; prohibit full-screen flashing, default per-second ticking, and per-second VoiceOver announcements.

answer.answer: RuptureOps can publicly distribute an independently authored, data-free app shell now, but not the current research corpus, imports, personalized material, or retained binary assets. Broader distribution requires source-owner reuse permission or replacement licensed data, plus independent clearance or replacement of all imagery, icon, and audio.

claims.value: The canonical source corpus remains private: SRDB permits crawling, but its footer asserts copyright and it publishes no explicit content/data reuse license. Therefore the raw RSC/static captures, normalized snapshots, generated SQLite knowledge base, all 1,081 indexed asset references, and privately mirrored binaries—including 466 available logical assets represented by 454 unique blobs—must not be republished without separate permission.

All personalized and imported material remains private. This includes the complete Star Rupture Game Analysis import and its raw ZIP/extracted corpus, legacy SQLite and reports; three user-authored prompt dumps totaling 58,207 bytes, 704 POSIX lines, 10,396 words, and 116 prompt delimiters; the structured player save and play-history models; consolidated player-specific vault notes; and nine player-specific site/geography assets. Promoted Ore Excavator v2 associations and consumable effects also retain imported, medium-confidence provenance and are not clean public-source substitutes.

A public build may presently use only independently authored application code and configuration, generic UI, and newly created or independently licensed assets, with all private data omitted. Current implementation evidence includes an iOS 17.0, Swift 6.0 project configured as RuptureOps 0.1.0 with application, unit-test, and UI-test targets, bundle ID com.rourkem.ruptureops, AppIcon, and AccentColor catalog slots. The benchmark fixture itself is not publishable and specifically retains binary site images, a generated app icon, and warning audio for a future multimodal lane; those retained binaries must stay private rather than being copied into the public build. The app must remain unofficial, avoid implying Creepy Jar endorsement, exclude hidden/prototype/stale play-test content from player-facing defaults, and expose material numerical version boundaries.

The safe distribution path is to create an explicit public allowlist containing only independently authored code/configuration and independently cleared assets, while excluding snapshots, SQLite, raw archives, imports, player models and notes, site images, the retained generated icon, and warning audio. Before distributing corpus-backed features more broadly, RuptureOps must either obtain separate reuse permission from the SRDB source owner or replace the corpus with a different licensed-data strategy. Images, icons, and audio additionally require their own documented permission/license or clean replacement. Public presentation must identify RuptureOps as unofficial and must not imply Creepy Jar endorsement.
